sources.notes: Previously used to study dense acoustic-guitar subdivision attacks and to correct evidence boundaries in the acoustic-strumming Skill. Keep source-specific content out of reusable Materials.

sources.title: Patience
sources.notes: Registered for later reference. Do not continue extracting reusable knowledge from this source while the current research focus is guitar strumming.

sources.title: Good Riddance (Time of Your Life)
sources.notes: Studied for reusable acoustic-strumming behavior only. Main guitar: GM program 24, 2048 notes, 684 exact onset groups, mostly 0.25/0.50-beat attack gaps, common 2-5-note attacks, and most 4/4 bars around 11-12 audible attacks on a sixteenth grid. User identified the rendered character as a useful common warm acoustic-strumming reference. Exact source rhythm, pitches and harmony are not stored in Materials.

sources.title: A Horse with No Name
sources.notes: Studied for rolling triplet acoustic-strumming behavior. Type-0 MIDI at 192 ticks per beat and 125 BPM. Main steel-string channel used GM program 25 and contained 3074 note-ons. Grouping adjacent note-ons within 12 ticks produced about 1015 strum groups with a median width of 3 notes. Attacks aligned overwhelmingly to beat starts and late-triplet positions. Beat-start groups with recoverable direction were strongly low-to-high, while late-triplet groups were almost entirely high-to-low. Within-stroke spread had a median around 20 ms and 90th percentile around 47.5 ms. Exact harmony, pitches and full source rhythm are not stored in Materials.

sources.title: Torn
sources.notes: Studied first as supporting evidence for warm-pop steel-string strumming, then separately for a more general pop-rock bass behavior. The bass used GM program 33 and contained 735 attacks. About 83% of adjacent attacks repeated the same pitch; 0.50- and 0.25-beat attack gaps dominated; many bars used about 9-10 attacks; bass attack positions strongly overlapped the main accompaniment rhythm while exact kick coincidence was much lower. This source motivated the normal-pop-rock-bass Material. Exact bass pitches, chord progression and full rhythmic masks remain source-specific.

sources.title: You Were Meant for Me
sources.notes: Studied for gentle steel-string strum-picking behavior. The MIDI is type 1 at 384 ticks per beat and about 111 BPM. Two long-running guitar channels used GM program 25. Channel 0 contained 490 note-ons from roughly beat 8 to 461 with median velocity about 72; channel 6 contained 896 note-ons from roughly beat 10 to 460 with median velocity about 55. After grouping close onsets, one channel was dominated by single-note attacks while the other mixed many single notes with many three-note partial groups. Common adjacent gaps were approximately 1/3, 2/3 and 1 beat. This source motivated the gentle-steel-strum-picking Material. Exact pitches, harmony and full rhythm remain source-specific.
